children: CEO Jensen Huang told employees during an all-hands meeting on Tuesday that he has started therapy and does not have a succession plan, according to
, which viewed video of his address to the company.
The meeting was held one day after Nvidia's founder was

as its CEO. He had resigned 12 days earlier after allegations of extramarital affairs surfaced, including with one woman accused of being a Chinese operative. The board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang following a series of discussions and meetings.
"I made some terrible mistakes," Huang said, according to the report. "I was unfaithful to Lori, and I hurt my kids, and of course, I hurt all of you."

Huang admitted his behavior was unacceptable, and he had violated the company's code of conduct. He also aimed to set the record straight on some allegations. He said the board did not reinstate him due to pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump.
"That is completely untrue," he said, according to the report.
He also said he wasn't reinstated because he was a "tech bro" who operates "above the law." Rather, the board evaluated the situation, gathered information, and did receive assurances from

that he was not a national security threat. Finally, he informed staff there is no succession plan in place, as he doesn't "believe in succession planning," as it could elevate some executives over others.
Nvidia was down 7.5% during afternoon trading on Tuesday following Monday's record-setting surge, in which the company added more than $1T in market capitalization.

title: Nvidia CEO says he has no succession plan during all-hands meeting: report
